lastReleaseMessage: v0.61.13.1 - the options file has never actually saved, restored identifiers are checked against their registry, the save format version starts moving again, and every silent null-texture branch says so once

items: Declared milestone moved M1 to M6 on 2026-08-26. M6 Art Integration is the track receiving the work and has been for weeks; M1 Vertical Slice stays open behind it. The old declaration paired M1 with a rule that the number only advances on a gameplay deliverable, which froze the number against a track nobody was on. The number now counts Roadmap deliverables across all nine milestones, so art work moves it.

How the 38 is derived, countable off the GDD Roadmap tab: 18 of 47 deliverables shipped. M0 8/8, M1 3/6, M2 2/4, M3 0/4, M4 2/6, M5 0/4, M6 3/5, M7 0/5, M8 0/5. Replaces the unsupported 50, which was hand-held since 2026-07-18 and disagreed with the document's own Progress tab aggregate of 34/135 (25 percent).

M1 Vertical Slice, three of six shipped and one previously mis-recorded. Open: Shambler + Lunger combat tuning, and Hatchery destruction + Coral Receding VFX (hatchery.gd is a scaffold with group membership, HP 800, a 2x2 footprint and four spawn constants; no spawn loop and no destruction handler exist). Mis-recorded: the Roadmap strikes 'Hold the Wall mission script (5-7 wave cadence)' as shipped, but source/data/missions/m1_default.tres is 'Mission 1: Hold the Line' at target_day 30, which against game_clock.DAY_LENGTH_SEC of 60 is a 30-minute mission with four horde nights at days 7, 14, 21 and 28. Neither a 5-7 wave slice nor the 5-7 minute mission M1's own target paragraph describes.

M6 Art Integration, three of five shipped. Building sprites, terrain tile set and HUD icon set are in. Open: unit sheets, where three of six scenes carry Spine rigs (scout, rifleman, marksman) and harpoonist, tommy and trench_sweeper carry none; and enemy sheets, where only the Shambler is rigged and the other seven are static single frames.

Live defect inside the active track: tools/bake_spine_sheets.gd configures two bakes, shambler and scout, while rifleman.tscn and marksman.tscn both carry rigs. Past the eight-unit LIVE_RIG_BUDGET in source/units/unit_lod.gd a demoted rig has no baked sheet to fall back to. Queued as bar-raise-2026-08-24-rising-asset-pipeline-01, which names the Rifleman only.

barRaise.topFinding: REDACTED: this run's top-finding narrative discusses a MED severity security-lens vulnerability. Full detail is in this project's own bar-raise report; withheld from the public copy.

actions.title: Route all four stamping functions through a temp write, rename and readback comparison, and re-run the integrity check after stamping rather than only before it.
Either add both unit types to the bake configuration so every rig-carrying unit has a fallback, or exclude units with no baked metadata from demotion and warn once per type when that happens.
Add both unit types to the bake configuration and commit their sheets before shipping the art milestone, or exclude both from the demotion candidate pool until baked sheets exist.

Rewrite that classifier to key off whether the unit scene carries a rig child, the condition that actually hides the body, then re-run the gate to confirm the marksman surfaces as a known bug or blocks until baked.

Add a dual-path hazard entry to this project's hazard catalog naming the two files, wire a project-scoped invocation of the parallel-implementation check into its own checks, and record the reacquire-interval divergence as an accepted difference so the check does not flag it as a regression.

Add a row for this project to the detection, location and release-command tables, or rewrite the release step to read the release script straight from the project context file instead of a per-project-name lookup.
Add a distinct row for this project to both the detection and release-command tables, keyed off the repository path rather than shared file markers.

Run the page updater after each release and commit the result, since the deploy workflow runs the same script without committing its output back, and replace the hand-typed homepage placeholder the script would never produce.
Rewrite that roadmap prose to match the live milestone and add a marker so the page updater can keep it current the way it already does for the sibling page.
Update the readme's status section to the current milestone, version and core mechanic, and fold that update into the release checklist so it does not drift again.
Run the scale benchmark against the current build and append a dated entry, or an explicit no-change note, so the log's claim of being the running record stays true.
Tag the inherited comments explicitly or renumber them into this project's own version line, so every in-code version reference resolves against one changelog.
Warn once when the shader update truncates at the cap, and put buildings before units or merge nearby sources so a late-game base does not lose visible clearing on its own structures first.
Add a superseded note to the older decision block or fold it into the newer entry, so the decisions tab gives one answer.
Scaffold the trigger points now, wired to placeholder or silent streams, so a composer delivery becomes an asset swap rather than new wiring under demo-prep pressure.
Re-verify the six deferred rows, confirm the original block still holds and restamp a dated reason, or close out any that no longer apply.
Either land the fifth-project change in that skill or rule explicitly that the digest stays four-project scoped and close the finding as will-not-do instead of leaving it open indefinitely.
Add an explicit wall-clock or token ceiling per project inside every shared-day slot so a long first-project fan-out cannot consume the second project's review budget.
Route the landing-page patch through the same temp file, rename and readback pattern already used for the store write in this script.
Extend the source integrity check, or add a small sibling check, to cover those two files and wire it into the pre-ship gate beside the existing ones.
Add a distinct row for this project to the commit-convention table instead of folding it under the combined row.
Either drop the restricted framing since the page is deliberately public marketing copy, or move its content behind the same server-side gate rather than a style toggle.
Route a publish failure to a durable channel, a notification or a queue item, and put the live gate freshness check on a recurring schedule instead of leaving it manual.
Add a row for this project to that table, matching or explicitly scoping down from the sibling's strictness given the same public publication.
REDACTED: a MED severity finding in the security lens is withheld from the public copy. See this project's own bar-raise report for detail.

Decide whether restricting outside readers is an actual goal; if it is, stop tracking the document in the pushed repository or ship a redacted build, and reword the readme so it does not call the gated copy a mirror of an open original.

Once the sync settles, run one playtest pass on enemy approach speed against the current numbers to confirm the three corrections converged on a value that plays right rather than one that merely matches the document.
Add sections for the three later milestones reconciled against the roadmap tab, matching the pattern already used for the earlier ones.
Convert those two sites to group-membership identity, or add a standing hazard line warning that any display-name rename must be checked against every string-equality site before shipping.
Add the missing token-shape patterns from the sibling's check, and decide deliberately whether to stay on the full-tree scan or move to the staged-diff scan.
Edit that entry to drop the collective pronoun and re-run the integrity check before the next publish.
Edit that entry so the sentence stays in one voice.
Rename both root nodes to match the naming convention the other unit scenes use.
Either extend the guard's lock list in the canonical copy and propagate it, or correct the runbook so it stops claiming coverage the guard does not have.
Have the fix log quote the finding id and a short excerpt inline instead of only the dated path, or have retention keep the audit and fix files for the same date as a pair.

Add an enemy class field to the stats resource and the shared numbers table, have the pooled getter read it instead of returning a literal, then correct the design document's divergence-closed claim once verified.
Have the overlay read the pool's alive count and its per-type breakdown instead of the per-node group alone.
Port the five-attempt write, read and verify retry block from the sibling's publish script into this one's landing-page write.

Rewrite that entry to describe the outcome without naming the review apparatus, and run the new pattern class against this document specifically, since it evidently was not run against this changelog before or after the row was added.

barRaise.reconcileNote: Reconciled both directions this run. Fourteen rows for this project sit blocked-on-user, the oldest thirty-six days, and six more have been deferred with no re-verification since 2026-06-23. Nothing closed on a queue status alone; every closure below rests on a lens re-reading the code this run.

closedLog.evidence: both rig types baked, imported and committed at 3072x1536 with seats inside the baker's valid range; the sheet check reads the row role order through an alias table and fails on an unknown name, proved by swapping two rows; the unbaked list is empty; v0.61.13 b331ef2

the baker's two outputs go through verified writers: temporary path, read back, compare dimensions or bytes, then rename; a failed readback removes the temporary and fails the bake; re-baked through the new path and the gate passes; v0.61.13

docs/ART_INTEGRATION_NOTES.md gained a rig delivery checklist: the six rows by role, the facing rule, the detached-art rule with the measured frame counts, the alpha rule, the no-fallback rule and the three commands; v0.61.13

save_load filters restored keeper, offer and research identifiers against each holder's own registry and warns naming what it dropped; a holder with no registry is trusted rather than emptied; v0.61.14
the save format version moves again, so the guard reading it has something to catch; v0.61.14

the version had sat at 1 through every field the payload gained; bumped to 2 with a version history and a recorded key set per version, and a test drives the real snapshot and fails on any added or removed key so the bump cannot be forgotten; v0.61.14

a test stages a stale truncated temporary file, calls the real options save, and asserts it returns true, leaves no temporary and leaves a file that reloads; writing it is what exposed the save that had never worked; v0.61.14

source/vfx/render_warn.gd, a preloaded library rather than an autoload so it adds no root path and no boot-order dependency, wired into the eight silent null-texture branches, once per distinct cause per run; v0.61.14
the load-failure signal carried a real cause and nothing listened; the screen flow now connects for the duration of the call, folds the reason into the toast and pushes a warning; v0.61.14

scripts/check_spine_versions.py asserts the runtime descriptor is present and tracked and that every library it names is present and tracked, with non-Windows entries declared absent by design; wired into the gauntlet; v0.61.14

the same gate reads the version stamped in every delivered skeleton header and the descriptor's minimum and compares both to the lock; it found seven of eight skeletons at 4.3.23 against a lock recording 4.3.17, the lock is corrected and the one remaining rig is named on every run; v0.61.14

the playtest caveat is in README.md under Status: no mission places a Hatchery, Brood Mound or Leviathan Cyst, so there is nothing to clear and pressure arrives only on the wave director's clock, which makes a run read as pure defence. The build half needs placement rules and a Coral Receding specification that do not exist, and is carried as rising-keeper-structures-reach-a-spawn-site-2026-09-02;

the per-Node fallback now has a test that keeps it honest: it pins that all eight flags exist and default on, that the wave director still reads every one, that each per-Node scene resolves and carries the fields the branch depends on, and that the dispatcher keeps a per-Node exit. Both pools also warn once when they grow past their pre-allocated records, because the renderers hold fixed buffers.

the cross-project digest reads its roster from the canonical status files instead of hardcoding four projects, which is the defect behind five consecutive runs of this finding; its description, its scope prose and its comparison table follow; both copies, 2026-09-02

both pools warn once when they grow past their pre-allocated records, naming that the renderer buffer does not grow with them so the overflow is live and undrawn; commit b2f78e3. The sizing half, clamping per-type growth against renderer capacity, is a design choice about what happens at the ceiling and is carried as rising-pool-renderer-capacity-clamp-2026-09-02

map_preview.tscn grounds on Plains512, the texture iso_grid.gd draws, at native scale with no scale constant left in the file, and the fifteen positions are a real diamond tiling rather than the untuned scatter they were; recorded in ART_INTEGRATION_NOTES.md including that the spacing is computed rather than judged by eye; commit 0b8ff83

the scale benchmark counts frames past twice each case's own median, prints the worst one, and prints the process, physics and draw reading from that exact frame, which is what makes a spike attributable to script, physics or render; helper behaviour proved against known data; commit 1f380b3
